title: Call audio on opus-pure: the voice codec, a jitter buffer and loss recovery
spec: docs/CALLS.md 'Opus: the crate, chosen by the conformance vectors'. A library crate on opus-pure (pinned), no audio device I/O. codec: VoiceEncoder::new(EncoderSettings) for 48 kHz mono, 20 ms frames (FRAME_SAMPLES 960), the VoIP application and the voice signal; EncoderSettings { bitrate 6000..=510000, complexity 0..=10, fec, expected_loss_percent 0..=100, dtx } defaults to 32 kbit/s, complexity 9, FEC on for 10 % loss, DTX off, and is checked (BadSetting); encode_f32 / encode_i16 take exactly one frame (FrameLength otherwise); set_settings refuses a bad value and changes nothing. VoiceDecoder: decode_f32 / decode_i16 of one packet (up to 120 ms), conceal_* for a lost packet (as long as the last one), recover_*(next) from the next packet's in-band FEC, reporting whether it carried a copy (has_fec: the LBRR flag of a SILK or hybrid packet's first frame, RFC 6716 4.2.4). Malformed packets are errors, never panics. jitter: JitterBuffer::new(depth >= 1, window in depth+1..=3000) keyed by 16-bit wrapping sequence numbers and RTP timestamps; push gives Queued, Duplicate, Late (its turn passed) or Resynced (more than window ahead: start again); pop starts once depth packets are held and gives the next turn in order: Packet, Lost (later packets are here; carries the next packet for FEC) or Underrun (nothing here; wait for it, stop after 5 in a row); counters for received, played, lost, late, duplicates, underruns, skipped. receiver: Receiver pushes packets and gives one Frame per tick (Decoded, Recovered or Concealed, with seq, timestamp and PCM); a packet that does not decode is concealed and counted. Test (relations, not values): a 440 Hz tone keeps its frequency within 1 % and level within 3 dB (f32 and i16); reordered packets come out in order; a lost packet is concealed without FEC and recovered with it, the recovered frame closer to the real one than concealment; a late packet is dropped; sequence numbers wrap and duplicates are ignored; random bytes, bit flips and truncations never panic the decoder or the receiver; settings are checked.
